stories.headline: CRPF DG visits Kulgam attack site, reviews operations as hunt for terrorists enters 3rd day
stories.title: CRPF DG visits Kulgam attack site, reviews operations as hunt for terrorists enters 3rd day
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 13: Director General of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), Gyanendra Pratap Singh, on Friday visited the site of the recent terror attack near Mir Bazar in Kulgam district and held detailed interactions with field officers of the CRPF and Jammu and Kashmir Police. The visit came as the joint hunt to track down the attackers entered its third consecutive day, with security forces continuing area-domination and search operations across the south Kashmir belt. During his visit to Kulgam in the Kashmir Valley, the DG CRPF took stock of the ground situation at the attack site in the Nowpora Akhran–Mir Bazar area. He later interacted with field officers of the CRPF and J&K Police at Sadura in Anantnag district, where discussions focused on the way ahead for intensified counter-insurgency (CI) operations in the Valley. The attack, which took place around 2:15 pm on Wednesday, targeted a CRPF checkpoint of the 46th Battalion deployed as a bridge guard roughly two kilometres off the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway. Preliminary investigations have indicated that at least three terrorists were involved, with two believed to be foreign nationals. Three CRPF personnel were injured in the firing. Two have since been discharged after treatment, while the third, who sustained wounds to the abdomen and spine, continues to receive care at the Army’s 92 Base Hospital in Srinagar. On Friday, joint teams of the Army, CRPF and J&K Police maintained an expanded cordon and continued combing operations in the forested and rural stretches around the attack site, while additional searches were underway at multiple locations across south Kashmir. Officials said several suspects were being questioned as part of the investigation, and technical and human intelligence inputs were being analysed to narrow down the movement of the attackers. Continuing his Kashmir Valley tour, Director General CRPF G P Singh, accompanied by senior CRPF officials, visited Head Constable (GD) Sonbir Singh, who is undergoing treatment at Army Hospital, Srinagar. Singh sustained serious injuries while displaying exceptional courage in repulsing a terrorist attack at Nowpora, Akhran in Kulgam on November 11, 2026. The DG CRPF lauded his courage and presence of mind, saying his swift retaliation foiled the terrorists’ designs and averted a major incident. He wished him a speedy recovery and also appreciated the Indian Army for providing prompt helicopter evacuation and quality medical treatment at the Army Hospital.

stories.headline: How French protests went out of control
stories.title: How French protests went out of control
stories.summary: PARIS: Smashed windows and ransacked shops. Bloodied teenage protesters. A city hall on fire.Such scenes shocked France as rioting erupted last month during nationwide protests over high living costs and strained ​public services.Government officials have repeatedly blamed far-left radicals and "opportunistic delinquents," who they say took advantage of mostly peaceful demonstrations to attack symbols of state authority and capitalism across France.Also read | A bitter African feud, a leadership battle and Macron's diplomatic tightrope in CambodiaBut the authorities' heavy-handed response - including thousands of arrests, police beatings and curbs on marches - has added to the volatile mix of grievances fueling an anti-government groundswell that shows no sign of abating before next year's presidential election, Reuters found.Reuters journalists reviewed dozens of videos of the violence, attended the court hearings of 26 people accused of taking part and interviewed over 50 government officials, police officers, attorneys, protesters and witnesses to understand how a movement that began in September with small protests over conditions in state schools spiraled into some of the worst civil unrest in years.Police tactics have faced scrutiny since the start due to the life-changing injuries suffered by some young people, including blown-off hands and lost eyes. United Nations and other human rights experts have also raised concerns about the arrest of nearly 7,000 minors during sometimes-violent school blockades, which they said was disproportionate.Images of riot police baton-charging teenagers fanned support for the students from a diverse array of protesters - including parents, teachers, left-wing politicians and trade unionists - who joined their marches."We have rights," said Emilie Berthier de Grandry, 42, who has attended four demonstrations in Paris with her 15-year-old son, Aaron, dressed in an inflatable shark costume. "We're not going to let ourselves be pushed around."Also read | Judo legend Teddy Riner's presidential bid faces a tough fight in FranceNationwide demonstrations on October 17 also brought a resurgence of so-called yellow-vest protesters, an anti-establishment movement that faced off against President Emmanuel Macron's government in 2018-2019 over high fuel prices.The violent outbursts were so intense that day that police lost control of entire neighborhoods to rioters and looters in France's three largest cities: Paris, Marseille and Lyon. Every week since then, people have taken to the streets across France to voice their anger at police and the government.While the protests after October 17 were calmer, clashes erupted when police sought to disperse demonstrators as marches wound down. Officers repeatedly fired tear gas and charged groups of protesters who pelted them with bottles, paving stones and mortar-style fireworks. On October 24, far-right gangs entered the fray saying they wanted to protect businesses and clashed with protesters in several cities, authorities said.The Interior Ministry, which oversees the police, said internal watchdogs have launched 161 investigations into allegations of officer violence against protesters since September.Responding to Reuters questions, the Interior Ministry said force is used in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.The minister, Laurent Nunez, has expressed regret for injuries caused by explosive weapons used in crowd control, including stun grenades. But he has resisted calls to ban them, saying security forces must be able to defend themselves.Nunez has acknowledged security lapses, telling lawmakers that authorities didn't anticipate the scale of the October 17 violence.He credits a massive security operation - including the deployment of 70,000 police officers and paramilitary gendarmes - for maintaining public order at subsequent protests. But he says security forces still face "a great deal of violence" at demonstrations, including a petrol-bomb attack that injured three gendarmes in Paris on Halloween.The unrest comes at a difficult time for Macron, who won't be standing for election again in April. Strained public finances leave him little room to meet protesters' demands, and his centrist party no longer has the majority needed to pass major legislation.Macron has promised to both "listen to the anger" and "impose respect of the Republican order."The government has sought to appease protesters with proposals to improve education and the decision to bring forward a planned minimum-wage increase. Student leaders and major trade unions say the moves don't go far enough and have vowed to keep up the pressure.AN ORCHESTRA HIT WITH TEAR GASOn October 17, protesters started gathering in Paris' Place de la Republique hours before a march was due to start at 2 p.m.Sousaphone in hand, Mael Roth arrived at about 11 a.m. for a warm-up session with the Orchestre du Nouveau Monde, a 400-piece classical orchestra that planned to perform in support of the marchers. The musicians were playing "The Avengers" theme song when the first clouds of tear gas wafted into the square about an hour later, the 20-year-old told Reuters.At first, he said, they assumed it wasn't aimed at them and kept playing. But within 30 minutes, tear gas canisters were landing at their feet.Reuters video shows riot police using tear gas around that time to drive back a group of protesters who tried to march down Rue du Faubourg du Temple, a street leading off the square.Elodie Aldila, who works at a patisserie on the street, welcomed the protection. Other businesses in the area were ransacked later that day.Roth, however, didn't see why the musicians couldn't remain in the square. Their aim was to "make people feel good," he said. "It was tough to feel ... like we're not legitimate."A huge crowd of mostly peaceful demonstrators soon filled the square again. But by then, the orchestra had packed up and left.POLICE OVERWHELMEDAs tensions built through the afternoon, bands of protesters spread into surrounding streets, smashing storefronts, erecting barricades and setting fire to cars and bicycles.Also read | JD Vance weighs 2028 presidential bid as Iran war and midterm losses cloud MAGA futureAround 4 p.m., police wielding batons beat a man to the ground after a heated exchange on the edge of the square, video verified by Reuters shows. Rumors of the man's death spread on social media, further inflaming tensions. The rumors later proved unfounded.An internal police watchdog is investigating the incident, the Interior Ministry said.As night fell, looting spread in Paris and other cities. Some 3,000 businesses were ransacked over 24 hours, from luxury boutiques to supermarkets.Addressing lawmakers last week, Nunez said an "unprecedented" mix of challenges unfolded simultaneously that day, overwhelming security forces.More than a half million people demonstrated around the country on October 17 - 110,000 in Paris alone, Nunez said. They included thousands of "ultra-left" activists, who he said confronted police from the start and tried to stage unauthorized marches toward seats of power.He didn't elaborate on the activists' suspected affiliations. French officials use the term ultra-left to describe a variety of groups, including anarchists and antifascists, who they say are willing to use violence.As word spread about the unrest on social media, people with no affiliation to such groups joined in the looting, Nunez said.In interviews with Reuters, three police officers and an intelligence official familiar with investigations into the violence said they couldn't confirm Nunez's assertions about the central role played by ultra-left groups. They said more investigation was needed to understand what happened."There is a body of circumstantial evidence but no certainty," said Eric Moulin, a regional representative of the UNSA Police union in Marseille.Asked about the assertion, the Interior Ministry referred Reuters to Nunez's previous remarks.Nunez and other officials have said rioters are using tactics promoted on ultra-left online platforms to provoke a police response. They include forming "black blocs," in which activists wear all-black clothing and conceal their faces, to attack businesses and public buildings, they said.HARDENED OFFICERS 'SCARED OUT OF THEIR MINDS'In Marseille, black-clad protesters broke into the city hall and toppled a bust of Marianne, a symbol of the French republic. Another group hurled rocks and steel bars at police at the Old Port, forcing around 45 officers to retreat to their vehicles and leave, verified videos show."Some of my colleagues who were inside the police vans said they felt so threatened they reached for their service weapons," Moulin said. "These are tough, hardened men, yet they confided in me that they were scared out of their minds."In Limoges, municipal police took cover inside the 19th-century city hall; rioters set it on fire. The officers escaped unharmed.The Lyon tourism office was also torched.Prosecutors are investigating charges of attempted murder against a 34-year-old carpenter suspected of helping start the Limoges fire. The city's mayor, Guillaume Guerin, told French TV the man is on a security watchlist for alleged ties to the ultra-left and was "most likely the mastermind of the operation."The suspect's lawyers said they had no such information. They urged the mayor to respect the presumption of innocence, saying the evidence against their client is weak.Prosecutors didn't answer Reuters questions about the case.4,900 SUSPECTS ARRESTED, MOSTLY YOUNG MENJustice Minister Gerald Darmanin has instructed prosecutors to deliver "an extremely firm judicial response" to the violence, including pre-trial detention and expedited trials for many accused.Over 4,900 suspects have been taken into custody since October 17, Darmanin told French TV on November 3. Some 2,290 were referred for prosecution and 404 handed prison sentences so far. Few details have been released about the suspects, though Darmanin said most are young men aged 18-25.The Tribunal de Paris, France's biggest courthouse, had to open two extra courtrooms for fast-track trials, which are reserved for people accused of low-level offenses. The schedule was so packed that some hearings Reuters observed had to be pushed back because the judge hadn't had time to review the case file.A union of French judges and prosecutors said it believes the justice system is being "instrumentalized" by the government. The Justice Ministry didn't respond to a request for comment.To avoid a repeat of the October 17 violence, the government reinforced police with troops at subsequent demonstrations, imposed curfews and banned numerous marches.Rights groups including Amnesty International have warned of a slide toward "authoritarianism." Officials said they were upholding the rule of law.Some researchers who study French social movements and policing have argued that the government's heavy-handed response is perpetuating the cycle of violence."Escalation happens when black blocs provoke with violence, and law enforcement are ordered to respond with violence," said Fabien Jobard, a sociologist at the French National Centre for Scientific Research.In this way, he said, groups are able to demonstrate that police are violent and attract support.Titouan Malin, an 18-year-old medical student, said he started volunteering as a medic at protests after seeing how police treated demonstrators on October 17."When you face this kind of violence - repression to such an extreme degree - you're forced to respond with violence," said Malin, who wore a white helmet and had a gas mask hanging around his neck as he watched for clashes during one of Paris' biggest marches on November 5."It's the only way to make ourselves heard."

stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin plan an unprecedented joint meeting on sidelines of APEC: officials
stories.title: Trump, Xi and Putin plan an unprecedented joint meeting on sidelines of APEC: officials
stories.summary: Washington, Nov 14: The leaders of the United States, China and Russia plan to meet Thursday on the sidelines of next week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China's tech hub of Shenzhen, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world's biggest nuclear powers. While the leaders gathering for joint talks will mark a singular moment, analysts say expectations are low that the talks will lead to major breakthroughs, and they will be heavier in symbolism than substance. Plans for the three-way summit with Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin were confirmed on Friday by the White House. It comes at a complicated moment in relations between the three countries. Trump has warmly embraced Xi after coming to a truce in their short-lived trade war last year and in spite of differences over the US war with Iran and other tensions between the world's foremost economic powers. Similarly, Trump has sought to build his relationship with Putin, even as the Russian leader has persisted in his nearly five-year-old war with Ukraine and as Moscow has deepened its military, intelligence and diplomatic partnership with Iran. The US president has insisted that such a meeting would provide an opportunity for the three leaders to discuss the US war with Iran and his goal of reaching a three-way agreement on their nuclear arms stockpiles. The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than a half-century. When that treaty -- known as New START -- expired, Trump rejected a call by Russia to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for “a new, improved and modernised” deal that includes China. But Beijing's arsenal of more than 600 warheads, according to Pentagon estimates, is far smaller than inventories held by the US and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads. With US and Russian arsenals dwarfing its stockpile, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact. Beijing was least certain about the value of the summit By agreeing to host the meeting, Xi may be calculating that the moment offers him an opportunity to flex China's growing clout and prestige. “I would be shocked if there were a joint statement that came out of this meeting that said anything about denuclearisation,” said Edgard Kagan, a former US ambassador to Malaysia who is now at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies. For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing. “I think the key for Putin was that this was very much about signalling a desire to talk to the president and talk to Chairman Xi in a way that suggests that they're making decisions on Ukraine, which obviously the Ukrainians and the Europeans don't like," Kagan said. The trilateral could very well overshadow the APEC summit. The summit, which is bringing 21 economies to Shenzhen, marks a big moment for China to show off its fast-growing, ultramodern coastal metropolis that transformed from a small fishing village into a global technology and economic hub in just a few decades. More substantively, such a gathering could also muddy China's argument that a Cold War mentality in the West was a contributing factor that led to Russia's war on Ukraine and its pointed criticism that the U.S. has undermined international institutions and treaties with how it has executed its war against Iran. The trilateral meeting could undercut China's push to portray itself as a defender of free trade at APEC, said Hoo Tiang Boon, a professor of Chinese foreign policy at Nanyang Technological University. “You sort of run counter to Chinese support of multilateralism,” he said. The leaders have met in pairs plenty of times over the years Putin and Xi are no strangers. They've fostered a close personal relationship, meeting more than 40 times since Xi became president in 2013 and addressing each other as “dear friend.” Trump and Putin have met face-to-face on seven different occasions, most recently in Alaska in August 2025. Xi and Trump have held face-to-face talks on eight occasions, including a September state visit to Washington by Xi. Beijing is the Number one trading partner for Moscow, a relationship that has strengthened since Putin sent troops into Ukraine in 2022. As the EU and the West sought to economically isolate Russia, China increased its purchases of Russia's energy resources and became Moscow's principal supplier of key technologies, including high-tech components for Russian weapons industries. Beijing has ignored Western demands to cut those supplies. In the lead-up to Russia's war on Ukraine, Xi and Putin declared their countries had a “no-limits friendship." China officially has said it is neutral on the conflict, while charging that Kyiv's Western allies played a part in provoking Russia's military action in Ukraine. Moscow, in turn, has repeatedly declared its support for Beijing's policy on issues related to Taiwan. Trump recently struck a diesel deal with Russia, waiving sanctions against Moscow and allowing for the sale of millions of tons of the fuel. The U.S. leader has blamed surging energy prices on Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries. Analysts, however, say the rise in global crude prices is due mostly to the Iran war. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concern that the trilateral meeting could serve as a platform for discussing a possible Ukraine deal behind Kyiv's back. Planning for the summit has drawn comparisons to the Yalta Conference, the 1945 gathering at which leaders of the US, Britain and the Soviet Union agreed to divide Germany and Berlin into four military occupation zones and finalised plans for establishing the United Nations. opening: Washington, Nov 14: The leaders of the United States, China and Russia plan to meet Thursday on the sidelines of next week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China's tech hub of Shenzhen, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world's biggest nuclear powers.

While the leaders gathering for joint talks will mark a singular moment, analysts say expectations are low that the talks will lead to major breakthroughs, and they will be heavier in symbolism than substance.
body: Plans for the three-way summit with Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin were confirmed on Friday by the White House.
It comes at a complicated moment in relations between the three countries.

Trump has warmly embraced Xi after coming to a truce in their short-lived trade war last year and in spite of differences over the US war with Iran and other tensions between the world's foremost economic powers.

Similarly, Trump has sought to build his relationship with Putin, even as the Russian leader has persisted in his nearly five-year-old war with Ukraine and as Moscow has deepened its military, intelligence and diplomatic partnership with Iran.

The US president has insisted that such a meeting would provide an opportunity for the three leaders to discuss the US war with Iran and his goal of reaching a three-way agreement on their nuclear arms stockpiles.
The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than a half-century.

When that treaty -- known as New START -- expired, Trump rejected a call by Russia to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for “a new, improved and modernised” deal that includes China.
But Beijing's arsenal of more than 600 warheads, according to Pentagon estimates, is far smaller than inventories held by the US and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads.
With US and Russian arsenals dwarfing its stockpile, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact.
Beijing was least certain about the value of the summit By agreeing to host the meeting, Xi may be calculating that the moment offers him an opportunity to flex China's growing clout and prestige.

“I would be shocked if there were a joint statement that came out of this meeting that said anything about denuclearisation,” said Edgard Kagan, a former US ambassador to Malaysia who is now at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies.
For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing.

“I think the key for Putin was that this was very much about signalling a desire to talk to the president and talk to Chairman Xi in a way that suggests that they're making decisions on Ukraine, which obviously the Ukrainians and the Europeans don't like," Kagan said.
The trilateral could very well overshadow the APEC summit.

The summit, which is bringing 21 economies to Shenzhen, marks a big moment for China to show off its fast-growing, ultramodern coastal metropolis that transformed from a small fishing village into a global technology and economic hub in just a few decades.

More substantively, such a gathering could also muddy China's argument that a Cold War mentality in the West was a contributing factor that led to Russia's war on Ukraine and its pointed criticism that the U.S. has undermined international institutions and treaties with how it has executed its war against Iran.

The trilateral meeting could undercut China's push to portray itself as a defender of free trade at APEC, said Hoo Tiang Boon, a professor of Chinese foreign policy at Nanyang Technological University.
“You sort of run counter to Chinese support of multilateralism,” he said.
The leaders have met in pairs plenty of times over the years Putin and Xi are no strangers.

They've fostered a close personal relationship, meeting more than 40 times since Xi became president in 2013 and addressing each other as “dear friend.” Trump and Putin have met face-to-face on seven different occasions, most recently in Alaska in August 2025.
Xi and Trump have held face-to-face talks on eight occasions, including a September state visit to Washington by Xi.
Beijing is the Number one trading partner for Moscow, a relationship that has strengthened since Putin sent troops into Ukraine in 2022.

As the EU and the West sought to economically isolate Russia, China increased its purchases of Russia's energy resources and became Moscow's principal supplier of key technologies, including high-tech components for Russian weapons industries.
Beijing has ignored Western demands to cut those supplies.

In the lead-up to Russia's war on Ukraine, Xi and Putin declared their countries had a “no-limits friendship." China officially has said it is neutral on the conflict, while charging that Kyiv's Western allies played a part in provoking Russia's military action in Ukraine.
Moscow, in turn, has repeatedly declared its support for Beijing's policy on issues related to Taiwan.
Trump recently struck a diesel deal with Russia, waiving sanctions against Moscow and allowing for the sale of millions of tons of the fuel.

Analysts, however, say the rise in global crude prices is due mostly to the Iran war.

stories.headline: J&K retail inflation climbs to 4.88% in October
stories.title: J&K retail inflation climbs to 4.88% in October
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 13: Retail inflation in Jammu and Kashmir accelerated to 4.88 percent in October 2026, up from 4.27 percent in September, extending the upward trend in prices for the sixth consecutive month and adding to the financial burden on households. According to the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), inflation in the Union Territory increased by 0.61 percentage points during October. The rate stood at 4.87 percent in rural areas and 4.91 percent in urban areas. The latest reading follows a steady increase in inflation since April, when the rate stood at 2.67 percent. It subsequently rose to 2.84 percent in May, 3.52 percent in June, 3.87 percent in July, 4.09 percent in August and 4.27 percent in September before reaching 4.88 percent in October. The increase in the official inflation rate comes amid concerns over the rising cost of essential commodities and the pressure on household budgets. The rural inflation rate increased from 4.12 percent in September to 4.87 percent in October, marking a rise of 0.75 percentage points. Urban inflation, meanwhile, increased from 4.65 percent to 4.91 percent during the same period. The figures indicate that rural areas witnessed a sharper acceleration in inflation than urban areas, although the overall rate remained marginally higher in urban areas. Despite the increase, J&K’s inflation rate remained below the national average of 6.09 percent in October. India’s retail inflation rose from 5.54 percent in September to 6.09 percent in October. Nationally, rural inflation stood at 6.63 percent, while urban inflation was recorded at 5.41 percent. At the national level, food inflation, measured through the Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), increased to 8.94 percent in October from 7.74 percent in September, indicating mounting pressure from food prices. Among individual commodities nationally, onion prices registered an annual increase of 116.22 percent, while garlic prices rose by 60.74 percent. Ginger and lemon prices increased by 48.32 percent and 47.30 percent, respectively. In contrast, potato prices declined by 14.24 percent and cauliflower prices fell by 10.57 percent. The national CPI data also showed that restaurants and accommodation services recorded inflation of 10.06 percent, while personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services registered inflation of 10.14 percent. However, these commodity-wise and category-wise figures are national estimates and do not represent individual inflation rates for Jammu and Kashmir. The October CPI figures are provisional and are based on the revised CPI series with 2024 as the base year. The National Statistics Office collected price data from 1,407 selected urban markets, including online markets, and 1,465 villages across the country. The CPI for November 2026 is scheduled to be released on December 14.

stories.headline: Div Com orders snow clearance, advance stocking in remote areas; 4x4 ambulances, 24x7 control rooms for winter
stories.title: Div Com orders snow clearance, advance stocking in remote areas; 4x4 ambulances, 24x7 control rooms for winter
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 13: Divisional Commissioner Kashmir Anshul Garg on Friday directed departments to ensure prompt snow clearance, advance stocking of essential commodities in remote areas and uninterrupted essential services as part of winter preparedness across Kashmir Division. Chairing a high-level meeting, Garg stressed coordinated efforts and timely response to minimise public inconvenience during the winter season. The meeting was attended by Deputy Commissioners, Commissioner Srinagar Municipal Corporation (SMC), Director Airport Authority Srinagar, SSP Traffic Rural and senior officers from KPDCL, R&B, MED, PMGSY, ULB, BRO, NHAI, Irrigation and Flood Control, PHE, IMD, FCS&CA, Health, SDA, Police and other concerned departments. Reviewing snow clearance action plans, the Divisional Commissioner directed MED, R&B, PMGSY, ULB, SMC and BRO to ensure prompt clearance of snow and clearly demarcate jurisdictional responsibilities to avoid duplication and confusion. He stressed optimal utilisation of available machinery and manpower and directed agencies to complete all pending stage contracts to strengthen the snow clearance mechanism. Chief Engineers and other officers informed the meeting that adequate arrangements were in place to ensure timely snow clearance on highways, major roads, streets and inner lanes immediately after snowfall. Reviewing winter power preparedness, Garg assessed electricity demand and supply, availability of buffer stocks of transformers, transformer oil, DG sets and HSD in Gurez, besides the status of branch cutting. The meeting was informed that all districts had adequate transformer stocks and 80 percent of branch cutting had been completed. It was further informed that average electricity demand in the Valley during winter was around 1,700 MW against an average supply of 1,300 MW, while peak demand touched 2,400 MW. The Divisional Commissioner directed the Chief Engineer, KPDCL, to augment workshop capacity wherever required, complete the remaining branch-cutting work at the earliest, strictly adhere to scheduled power curtailment timings and ensure prompt repair of damaged transformers. Reviewing the availability of essential commodities in remote and snowbound areas, including Gurez and the Karnah-Machil-Keran belt, he directed FCS&CA to complete advance stocking of LPG, petroleum products, rice and wheat within a week. He stressed that adequate stocks be maintained in all far-flung areas to prevent shortages and inconvenience to the public during road closures. Taking note of delays in the commencement of winter air sorties in Bandipora and Kupwara, Garg directed the Civil Aviation Department to operationalise the facility by December 1 to facilitate emergency transportation from remote and inaccessible areas. Regarding flight operations at Srinagar Airport, he directed the Director, Airport Authority Srinagar, to ensure timely dissemination of information to passengers and the general public about changes in flight schedules due to adverse weather conditions. The Divisional Commissioner also reviewed healthcare preparedness across districts, including heating arrangements in hospitals, availability of essential medicines, deployment of medical staff in far-flung areas and the requirement for 4x4 ambulances. He directed the National Health Mission (NHM) to provide 4x4 ambulances to the Directorate of Health Services Kashmir for distribution among districts, in addition to SANJY ambulances. Emphasising proactive healthcare arrangements, Garg directed the Health Department to undertake comprehensive line-listing of expectant mothers and critically ill patients in vulnerable and remote areas. He also stressed advance shifting of such patients to temporary shelters, wherever required, to ensure uninterrupted access to medical care during heavy snowfall and road closures. Reviewing the preparedness of the Jal Shakti Department, he directed officials to ensure uninterrupted functioning of all PHE schemes, including lift water supply schemes, and make adequate arrangements for deploying water tankers wherever required to ensure drinking water availability. He also directed the Forest Department to ensure adequate stocking of firewood at depots across the Valley. To strengthen interdepartmental coordination, Garg directed all district administrations and departments to ensure round-the-clock functioning of their respective control rooms, including the Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC). He also instructed departments to appoint nodal officers and share their contact details to facilitate timely assistance, coordination and dissemination of information. Stressing the importance of timely weather-related advisories, he directed concerned departments to promptly share weather and avalanche forecasts with the public to minimise risks and safeguard lives. Meanwhile, he directed the Commissioner, SMC, to identify waterlogging hotspots across Srinagar city and ensure deployment of adequate dewatering pumps to address any eventuality during winter. The Divisional Commissioner also emphasised accountability and timely grievance redressal, directing officers to properly document the time of occurrence of any issue and the response time taken by the concerned department to resolve it. During the meeting, Deputy Commissioners briefed the chair about winter preparedness measures undertaken in their respective districts and highlighted critical issues requiring intervention and resolution. Garg called upon all departments to maintain close coordination and ensure that necessary arrangements were put in place well in advance to minimise public inconvenience and ensure the safety and well-being of people across Kashmir Division during the winter season.

stories.headline: India Shines at Youth Olympics with Historic 10-Medal Haul, Including Two Golds
stories.title: India Shines at Youth Olympics with Historic 10-Medal Haul, Including Two Golds
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: New Delhi: India signed off from the 2026 Summer Youth Olympic Games in Dakar with 10 medals, including two gold, three silver and five bronze, marking the country’s second-best performance in the history of the competition.
India’s medal-winning campaign spanned seven disciplines, with five Khelo India Athletes among the medallists.
They included Tanvi Patri (Badminton), Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada (Judo), Shourya Ambure (Athletics), Gunjan (Boxing) and Tirthank Pegu (Swimming).

Nine of India’s 17 athletes returned with medals, while swimmer Dhinidhi Desinghu created history by becoming the first Indian athlete to win two medals in a single edition of the Youth Olympic Games.
India’s 10-medal tally was surpassed only by its 13-medal performance at the 2018 Youth Olympics.
Boxing emerged as India’s biggest success story, with Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei winning gold in the boys’ 50kg category and Gunjan claiming the top podium finish in the girls’ 48kg category.
The two victories gave India its first-ever gold medals in boxing at the Youth Olympic Games and marked the country’s first boxing gold double at the competition.
With two gold medals, India also recorded its second-highest gold medal tally in a single edition of the Youth Olympic Games.
The campaign also witnessed several historic achievements across other disciplines.
Shourya Ambure became the first Indian athlete to win an athletics medal at the Youth Olympic Games, claiming bronze in the girls’ 100m hurdles.
Taniya secured silver in girls’ freestyle 75kg beach wrestling, giving India its first-ever medal in the discipline at the competition.
India also registered its first medals in swimming and Wushu at the Youth Olympics.
